psalm_response: I will seat the victor beside me on my throne.
homily:
In the Book of Revelation, we hear the Lord speaking to the Church in Laodicea, and He says something that strikes us right at the heart of our own quiet, sometimes hidden lives: 'Behold, I stand at the door and knock.' It is a beautiful image, isn't it? The Lord of the Universe, the one who holds the seven stars, does not kick down the door of our hearts. He does not force His way into the rooms where we keep our sorrow, our confusion, or our deepest memories. He stands. He knocks. He waits. He waits for us to be ready to open the door, even just a crack, to let the light of His presence spill into the places where we have been sitting in the dark.

Think of the sycamore tree in the Gospel. Zacchaeus, a man of stature and wealth, but one who felt the ache of being 'short'—not just in height, but perhaps in his standing before God—climbs that tree. He wants to see. He wants to know if this Jesus, the one everyone is talking about, is real. He is desperate for a glimpse. And Jesus, as He passes by, does not look at the crowd. He does not look at the people grumbling about who He is spending time with. He looks up. He sees the one who is seeking. He calls him by name: 'Zacchaeus, come down quickly, for today I must stay at your house.'

There is a profound, quiet truth here for all of us, especially you, Alan and Thao, and you, Ryan. We often think that we must be the ones to reach up, to climb the highest tree, to be the strongest or the most faithful, in order to catch the attention of God. We think we have to earn the visit. But the Gospel shows us that the initiative belongs to Him. He is the one who comes to Jericho. He is the one who stops. He is the one who says, 'I must stay at your house.'

Benjamin was a boy who understood this kind of movement. He was a boy who loved the way things were built—the logic of a line of code, the precision of a jet engine, the way a dream like 'Con Chim Airlines' could bring a smile to his face and to yours. He had a brilliant mind, yes, but he had something even more precious: a heart that was always open to the 'next thing.' He was always looking toward the horizon, always curious, always ready to see what was around the next corner. That curiosity was not just for the world; it was a reflection of a soul that was made for the infinite.

When we look at the photo of nine-year-old Ben, wrapped around a younger child near the Christmas tree, wearing his silver cross, we see the truth of his life. He was a boy who carried the light of Christ in his very posture. He did not need to speak a word to show that he was a 'victor,' as the Psalm says—the one who walks blamelessly and thinks the truth in his heart. He simply was. He was a boy who knew that the most important things in life are not the things we possess, but the ways we offer ourselves to one another. Like the time he offered his entire piggy bank to his uncle—that moment wasn't about the money. It was about the reach of his love. It was about a boy who looked at the suffering of someone he cared about and wanted to give everything he had to make it better. That is the heart of the Gospel. That is the heart of the Kingdom.

I know that for some of you, the door feels heavy these days. You feel like the church in Sardis—you have a reputation for being alive, but you feel like you are just going through the motions, trying to keep the fire burning when you feel so tired. You wonder if your works are complete, or if you have somehow fallen short. But listen to what the Lord says to those who have not soiled their garments: 'They will walk with me dressed in white, because they are worthy.' You are not being judged by your exhaustion. You are being held by the one who knows your name.

There is a special comfort for those who feel they might have missed something, who look back at the past and wonder if they could have done more. The Gospel of Luke is very clear: 'The Son of Man has come to seek and to save what was lost.' It does not say that He comes to judge the parents, or to blame the ones who loved the most. It says He comes to seek. He is the one doing the seeking. If you are feeling that weight of 'what if,' I want you to hear this clearly: you are not the one who failed. You are the one who was loved, and who loved in return. God does not hold your heart to a standard of perfection; He holds it in a standard of mercy. The sorrow you carry is not a sign of your failure; it is a sign of how deeply you have loved. And love, in the eyes of God, is never wasted. It is the only thing that lasts.

Think of the way Ben lived. He was a boy who shared his joy. Whether he was 'airport spotting' with his dad or just giggling about his airline, he was a boy who invited others into his world. He didn't keep his happiness to himself. He made it a shared experience. That is what we are called to do today. We are called to share the joy that Ben brought into our lives. We are called to be the ones who keep the 'Well of Love' flowing, not just in Cà Mau, but in the way we treat the people we meet today. When you see someone who is struggling, someone who feels like they are on the outside looking in, be the one who looks up. Be the one who says, 'I see you.'

Ryan, my dear brother, you have a legacy that is yours alone. You and Ben were a team. You shared the roller coasters, the dreams, the laughter. That connection is not a memory that fades; it is a thread that runs into eternity. You are carrying the best part of your brother in your own heart. When you are kind, when you are curious, when you push yourself to try your best, you are keeping that spirit alive. You are the one who knows his smile the best, and you are the one who can help that smile continue to shine in this world.

Alan and Thao, the Lord is standing at the door of your home. He is not there to ask for an explanation. He is there to dine with you. He is there to sit at your table, to share the silence, to be the guest who understands the ache of the empty chair. You don't have to be 'hot' or 'cold' for Him. You can be exactly where you are. You can be tired. You can be sad. You can be wondering. He is the 'Amen,' the faithful and true witness. He is the one who knows your story from the very first page to the very last. And He is telling you, just as He told Zacchaeus, that salvation has come to your house. Not because you were perfect, but because you were His.

There is a promise in the Book of Revelation that we must hold onto: 'I will never erase his name from the book of life but will acknowledge his name in the presence of my Father and of his angels.' Benjamin Vo is not a name that is fading. It is a name that is written in the light. It is a name that is being spoken in the courts of Heaven. He is there, and he is waiting. He is watching over you with that same gentle, radiant spirit that he always had. He is not 'gone' in the way we fear; he is simply part of the great cloud of witnesses that is cheering for you as you run the race.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Carry the peace of knowing that you are not alone. Carry the memory of a boy who wanted to give everything he had to help his uncle, and let that inspire you to give a little bit of yourself to someone else today. It doesn't have to be big. A kind word, a moment of patience, a prayer for someone who is hurting—these are the ways we keep the 'Well of Love' flowing. These are the ways we show the world that death does not have the final word. Love does. And the love that you shared with Benjamin is a love that will never, ever end. He is safe. He is home. And you, in your own time, are being led there too, one step, one day, one prayer at a time. Trust in the one who stands at the door. He is already inside, and He is holding you, and your boy, in the palm of His hand. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you in His light, now and forever. Amen.

Kikkut nalligijavut uqumaittumik atuqtut, ataniup qanigillugu, nalligivikluq inuusiup iluani.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text: I, John, heard the Lord saying to me: “To the angel of the Church in Sardis, write this: ‘The one who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars says this: “I know your works, that you have the reputation of being alive, but you are dead. Be watchful and strengthen what is left, which is going to die, for I have not found your works complete in the sight of my God. Remember then how you accepted and heard; keep it, and repent. If you are not watchful, I will come like a thief, and you will never know at what hour I will come upon you. However, you have a few people in Sardis who have not soiled their garments; they will walk with me dressed in white, because they are worthy. The victor will thus be dressed in white, and I will never erase his name from the book of life but will acknowledge his name in the presence of my Father and of his angels. Whoever has ears ought to hear what the Spirit says to the churches.’” “To the angel of the Church in Laodicea, write this: ‘The Amen, the faithful and true witness, the source of God’s creation, says this: “I know your works; I know that you are neither cold nor hot. I wish you were either cold or hot. So, because you are lukewarm, neither hot nor cold, I will spit you out of my mouth. For you say, ‘I am rich and affluent and have no need of anything,’ and yet do not realize that you are wretched, pitiable, poor, blind, and naked. I advise you to buy from me gold refined by fire so that you may be rich, and white garments to put on so that your shameful nakedness may not be exposed, and buy ointment to smear on your eyes so that you may see. Those whom I love, I reprove and chastise. Be earnest, therefore, and repent. Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will enter his house and dine with him, and he with me. I will give the victor the right to sit with me on my throne, as I myself first won the victory and sit with my Father on his throne. Whoever has ears ought to hear what the Spirit says to the churches.”

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text: R. I will seat the victor beside me on my throne. He who walks blamelessly and does justice; who thinks the truth in his heart and slanders not with his tongue. R. I will seat the victor beside me on my throne. Who harms not his fellow man, nor takes up a reproach against his neighbor; By whom the reprobate is despised, while he honors those who fear the LORD. R. I will seat the victor beside me on my throne. Who lends not his money at usury and accepts no bribe against the innocent. He who does these things shall never be disturbed. R. I will seat the victor beside me on my throne.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text: At that time Jesus came to Jericho and intended to pass through the town. Now a man there named Zacchaeus, who was a chief tax collector and also a wealthy man, was seeking to see who Jesus was; but he could not see him because of the crowd, for he was short in stature. So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree in order to see Jesus, who was about to pass that way. When he reached the place, Jesus looked up and said, “Zacchaeus, come down quickly, for today I must stay at your house.” And he came down quickly and received him with joy. When they saw this, they began to grumble, saying, “He has gone to stay at the house of a sinner.” But Zacchaeus stood there and said to the Lord, “Behold, half of my possessions, Lord, I shall give to the poor, and if I have extorted anything from anyone I shall repay it four times over.” And Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house because this man too is a descendant of Abraham. For the Son of Man has come to seek and to save what was lost.”

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
